newsitem.title: USA: Calif. fund reviews Nomura Securities ties.
newsitem.headline: Calif. fund reviews Nomura Securities ties.

text.p: California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS) said Monday it would review its business ties with Nomura Securities Co Ltd after the broker revealed suspected illegal trades.
"We're reviewing the situation to determine whether any action needs to take place," said CalPERS spokesman Brad Pacheco. "But we're far from making a decision."
New York-based Nomura Capital Management Inc, a Nomura Securities affiliate, manages about $724 million of the California pension fund's assets, Pacheco said.
A Nomura Capital official declined to comment Monday.
Some investment management companies said they would suspend business dealings with Nomura Securities from Monday following news that two of its directors were involved in suspected illegal deals.

Pacheco said CalPERS would review these developments to determine whether the pension fund's assets would be impacted. This review could take several months, he said, adding that the results of the review could prompt CalPERS to take action.
"We could take several actions, from nothing to placing the manager on a watch list, to probation or termination," Pacheco said.

CalPERS is the largest public employee pension system in the United States with more than $108 billion in assets. The pension system manages retirement and health plans for more than one million California public employees, retirees and their families.
